newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas prices hold ahead of outage.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices hold ahead of outage.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices remained firm Friday as a scheduled outage in Alberta kept supplies tight, traders said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was discussed again at C$1.58-1.59 per gigajoule.
August AECO was quoted at C$1.53-1.54.
A maintenance outage on NOVA Gas Transmission's Grande Prairie mainline in northern Alberta is expected to take about about one billion cubic feet per day off the system from Sunday through Thursday.
Canadian Gas Association (CGA) reported earlier today that gas stocks for the week ended July 4 were at 201.81 bcf, or 41.2 percent full, versus 43.3 percent a year ago.
In the West, stocks were at 122.5 bcf, or 42.8 percent full. For the same week a year ago, stocks were 51 percent of capacity, CGA said.
At Sumas, Wash., prices also held steady around $1.20 per million British thermal units as some western buying came to a halt for the weekend.
Spot prices in the Permian basin fell four cents to about $2.02, traders said.
At Niagara, prices were quoted steady to higher at $2.30-2.32 per mmBtu as temperature highs in Toronto hovered around 80 degrees F.
CGA reported that eastern Canadian stocks were at 79.32 bcf, or 29.2 percent full, versus 34.1 percent a year ago.
